method: Triage of the ThirdCheck static analyzer output over the cloned submission repositories. Each raw signal is classified by evidence and file path. 'confirmed' = a production, source-visible binding defect. 'review' = a real production pattern whose severity needs the call site / access control read before any claim. 'noise' = test/mock code or off-chain catch-return-null no contract consumes. Named report; the private basis for responsible disclosure, not for publication.

findings.title: Verification via a selector the precompile does not implement
findings.note: verifySingle is an SDK method name, not an on-chain selector. The precompile exposes only verify, verifyAndEmit, calculateTxIndex. A contract calling verifySingle at 0x0FD2 cannot reach the real precompile.
findings.reason: VaultLending._verifySingle calls IUSCVerifier(target).verifySingle at 0x0FD2 on every registration path; verifySingle is not a precompile selector, so real inclusion+continuity verification is never reached

findings.reason: verifyBatch is not a precompile selector; the batch registration path calls it at 0x0FD2 and cannot reach real verification

findings.title: A mock verifier is present in the source tree
findings.note: A mock is fine for tests. Combined with a swappable verifier address it is the mechanism by which a deployed demo can bypass the real precompile. Confirm production never points the verifier here.

findings.title: Verifier address is swappable after deployment
findings.note: The verifier target lives in mutable storage. If the owner can point it at a mock, on-chain verification is decorative. Address the precompile as an immutable constant instead.
findings.reason: verifier target in mutable storage; severity depends on access control (owner/timelock/multisig) — needs the setter's guard read

findings.title: Verifier address is swappable after deployment

findings.reason: setVerifier is onlyOwner with no write-once/timelock guard; owner (EOA) can point verifierAddress at MockStreakPrecompile (shipped in src/, returns true), making verification decorative

findings.title: Generator returns null on failure, read upstream as absence
findings.note: A scan that throws and returns null cannot be distinguished from a scan that found nothing. If null means 'no payment' anywhere upstream, a dead RPC manufactures a negative result.
findings.reason: catch-return-null in off-chain app code; not a contract treating absence as proven

findings.title: Generator zeroes the proof on failure but still reports success
findings.note: The proof generation failed, the proof was blanked, and the result still claims success. A consumer trusting that flag acts on an empty proof.
findings.reason: generator zeroes the proof on failure but returns success; a consumer acts on an empty proof
